hints.title: Interval Sorting Strategy
hints.text: Sort intervals primarily ascending by end point, and secondarily descending by start point.

hints.title: Greedy Rightmost Placements
hints.text: Placing numbers as far to the right as possible within an interval maximizes their ability to intersect future intervals.

hints.title: Track Two Largest Chosen Elements
hints.text: Maintain the two largest elements chosen so far, say p1 and p2 with p1 < p2. If the current interval contains neither, add end minus 1 and end. If it contains only p2, add end. Update p1 and p2 accordingly.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def intersectionSizeTwo(self, intervals: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        intervals.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1], -x[0]))
        p1, p2 = -1, -1
        ans = 0

        for s, e in intervals:
            if s > p2:
                p1 = e - 1
                p2 = e
                ans += 2
            elif s > p1:
                p1 = p2
                p2 = e
                ans += 1

        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Greedy sorting by interval endpoint tracking the two highest chosen elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Set cover formulation without interval ordering is NP-hard in general graphs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting intervals enables greedy selection in O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sort secondary start descending so shorter intervals ending at the same point are processed first.
